chapter: Berlin and the Turner and Bryant bands
title: Germany in 1933: Hitler, marks and no race problem
summary: Butler says he did not follow politics, just got paid in marks, and met no racial problem in Germany; he joined Charlie Turner's band.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, how long were you in Europe?
Yeah, I didn't get a chance to -- is this 1933?
Okay, now Hitler had just become Chancellor then. Or was on his way.
Well, see, I didn't know that much about politics to really note. (Inaudible). All I know, that money was flowing and I was getting them marks and I was doing good.
Now, you didn't have any kind of racial problem there?
Oh, no, no, no. That wasn't a risk because I was what I am, what I was. There wasn't no race about it. That term wasn't there.
No, it just wasn't there. It wasn't there. It was not there. It was a beautiful scene. (Inaudible). And I joined, as I said, Charlie Turner's band.
